author: Cheung Hok-hang
description:
The Shenzhen Natural History Museum will open to the public on July 28 as the first dedicated large-scale institution of its kind in southern China.
Spearheaded by the Shenzhen government with a total investment of 3.5 billion yuan (US$517 million) – excluding the cost of collecting artefacts – the museum, located in the Pingshan district in the northeast of the city, is among its “Ten Cultural Facilities of the New Era”.
The first of these to open was the new Shenzhen Art Museum in 2023,...
title: What to see at the Shenzhen Natural History Museum, from dinosaur fossils to meteorites

author: Göktuğ Çalışkan
description:
When Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), met Jiang Feng, head of China’s mission to the African Union, in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in mid-July, the message was practical. They signed a handover certificate that brought Beijing’s direct emergency support for the Ebola response to US$4.5 million. A five-member Chinese medical team was already working in the Democratic Republic of Congo capital of Kinshasa.
Kaseya described the contribution as...
title: With rapid Ebola aid, China shows itself a reliable partner of Africa

author: Han Li
description:
A congressional advisory panel focused on China has returned from a trip to Beijing, Shanghai and Hangzhou, with commissioners pledging to make the visits an annual event to strengthen engagement and inform their work on US-China relations.
The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC), an independent advisory body established in 2000, provides annual reports and recommendations to lawmakers on trade and national security-related policies.
“We are committed to seeking to return at...
title: US congressional group plans annual visits to China after trade trip

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva agreed on Sunday night to accelerate negotiations for a trade agreement between China and Mercosur, a striking reversal for Brasilia, which for years led resistance to such a deal in the South American bloc.
The two leaders spoke by telephone for more than an hour, according to a statement from the Brazilian presidency, and “coincided on the importance of speeding up the talks for a Mercosur-China agreement that...
title: Brazil turns to China trade deal after Trump’s tariffs, as years of resistance end

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
With less than three months to go until Brazil’s presidential election, China is closely watching a high-stakes political duel between a Beijing-friendly incumbent and his pro-Washington challenger.
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who maintains close ties with Beijing, is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term.
His rival, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro – son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who was jailed last year for attempting a military coup – was confirmed on Saturday as the...
title: Trump, tariffs and ties with China at stake in Brazilian presidential race

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Chinese researchers have completed trials of a new rare earth-based synthetic rubber production facility, industrialising a major raw material for manufacturing electric vehicle and heavy-duty vehicle tyres.
High-quality synthetic rubber, most of which uses metal as a catalyst during production, is vital to the transport industry, manufacturing and national defence.
The unit, built by Xinjiang-based PetroChina subsidiary Dushanzi Petrochemical with support from the Changchun Institute of Applied...
title: Why use rare earths in rubber production? Chinese scientists are engineering tougher tyres

author: Syed Munir Khasru
description:
South Asia is undergoing a gradual but important shift. Smaller states now command a widening array of options, and India’s primacy is quietly giving way. The lesson is clear. Regional leadership can no longer rest on geography and must be sustained through credible and mutually beneficial engagements that compare favourably with the alternatives.
China’s challenge begins at India’s border. Both countries fought in 1962, continue to dispute a frontier of roughly 3,500km and had their deadliest...
title: India is losing its regional primacy as Beijing and Washington move in

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taipei mayor Wayne Chiang Wan-an has emerged as the biggest political winner from an opposition protest against the government’s handling of a food safety scandal that drew what organisers said were more than 200,000 people onto the streets of the city.
The unexpectedly large turnout on Saturday appears to have given the island’s main opposition party, the Kuomintang, fresh momentum ahead of the local elections in November, and could reshape the race to become the party’s candidate in the next...
title: Will the heat from a cooking oil scandal help the opposition in Taiwan?

author: Albee Zhang
description:
Alleged scam-network mastermind Chen Zhi could face the death penalty, with Chinese prosecutors adding intentional injury to the list of charges against him.
Chen, 38, was extradited from Cambodia to China six months ago and formally arrested on July 6, according to Chinese business magazine Caixin.
He founded the Cambodian conglomerate Prince Group, which authorities say was linked to a sprawling online scam network.
Caixin reported on Monday that prosecutors dropped a previous count of...
title: China charges alleged scam kingpin Chen Zhi with intentional injury: report

author: Orange Wang
description:
Beijing is stepping up its global messaging campaign over East China Sea islets that Tokyo also claims by rolling out a five-part documentary to tell its version of history.
The state broadcaster’s English-language channel, China Global Television Network (CGTN), released the first part of Diaoyu Dao: Small Islands, Big Stakes on Monday to “examine the history, legal debates and contemporary realities” surrounding the group of small, uninhabited islands, which Japan administers as the...
title: Beijing fires new salvo at Tokyo with documentary on disputed Diaoyu Islands

author: Victoria Bela
description:
After decades of fighting desertification with straw, plants and plastic, Chinese researchers have turned to bamboo – one of the most resilient and sustainable materials on the planet.
The fastest-growing plant on Earth has the potential to help overcome challenges with current sand-fixing methods including short lifespan, ecological risks and health issues.
Beijing on July 22 released a five-year conservation plan for the country’s forests and grasslands, which includes projects to be...
title: Chinese scientists turn to bamboo to strengthen the Great Green Wall

author: Dannie Peng
description:
China’s agriculture sector needs more advanced technology and innovation to boost yields and improve food security – not more farmland and crops, according to a rural policy expert.
The remarks came after a state media investigation alleged that officials in central China had inflated the size of mandatory rice crops to hit their targets.
CCTV programme Focus Report aired its investigation on July 14, claiming officials in Jianghua Yao – a county in Yongzhou, Hunan province – had misreported the...
title: Food security: can drones and BeiDou put an end to ‘paper farming’ in China?

author: Natalie Wong
description:
When Zhou Yuxiang, founder and CEO of Shanghai-headquartered Black Lake Technologies, wanted to sell his artificial intelligence (AI) automation solutions to millions of family-run factories across China, he came up with an unconventional strategy: hiring food delivery workers to make sales.
His entire sales team, hired from various industrial cities, survived a gruelling five-day boot camp on articulating how AI can solve specific manufacturing pain points.
“They are very street-smart,” the...
title: Black Lake CEO’s strategy to sell AI solutions to factories: turn to food couriers

author: Caroline Lin
description:
Chinese scientists have developed a way to create clothing and textiles from a fungus that can self-clean and regenerate.
The fabric can also be customised – for example to add colour or protect the wearer from ultraviolet (UV) rays – with the help of other microorganisms, according to a study published on Friday.
A persistent challenge for engineered living materials (ELMs) has been scaling up microscopic living cells into large, durable structures that remain alive and functional.
A research...
title: From fungus to fashion: Chinese scientists develop sustainable ‘living textiles’

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
The United States has spent decades trying to blunt China’s strategic rise. Yet in the Middle East, sanctions and the war against Iran are now dismantling one of the few assets built to constrain Beijing’s influence in the region.
The Iranian port of Chabahar has received strong backing from India, which hoped it would gain both a trade corridor into Afghanistan and Central Asia that bypassed Pakistan and a strategic counterweight to the Chinese-operated Pakistani port of Gwadar.
Both Washington...
title: How Trump’s Iran ‘own goal’ is hitting long-term US strategy to contain Chinese influence
